description.narrative: Public participation is the backbone of social accountability. To increase public participation, citizens need to feel that their participation contributes to holding the government accountable and improving their openness and performance. Therefore, it is crucial to work on the capacity and enabling environment for the CSOs/CBOs, youth, and municipalities to enhance citizens participation in decisionmaking at the local level and increase their engagement in social accountability activities in output two. This output will focus on revising existing governmental tools such as MoLAs Methodology for the development of local needs plans with a focus on CSOs roles and their contribution to policy change at a local level. This also includes CSOs/CBOs role in improving municipalities budget and expenditure efficiency, transparency, effectiveness, and accountability and ensuring equitable distribution of public finances for both women and men by disseminating the culture and practice of genderresponsive budgeting. The project will also develop various manuals and templates based on the local context and best practices to organize public hearings and social accountability sessions.Additionally, since social accountability is built on public participation, the citizens must engage in discussing their needs, issues, and performance of their public servants using numerous tools that will enhance their capacity to hold the government accountable. Therefore, an annual survey will be conducted in 10 municipalities to identify the citizens concerns regarding public issues and measure citizens satisfaction with the municipalities performance. This will enhance the transparency of the municipalities towards the citizens and can be used to monitor the projects performance.entre.
